newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Perry to watch Russians destroy nuclear submarine.
newsitem.headline: Perry to watch Russians destroy nuclear submarine.

text.p: U.S. Defence Secretary William Perry was due to visit a northern Russian naval base on Friday to watch the destruction of Russian submarines under the START-1 nuclear arms reduction pact.

Perry, senior U.S. defence officials and three U.S. senators were to drive from from the port city Arkhangelsk to the frigid secret base at Severodvinsk, where giant Soviet nuclear missile submarines were built during the Cold War.
The visit was similar to one paid by Perry last year to Engels Air Base south of Moscow where he saw the destruction of Soviet long-range bombers under the START-1 treaty.
Accompanying Perry to Severodvinsk were Democratic U.S. Senators Sam Nunn of Georgia and Joseph Lieberman of Connecticut and Republican Senator Richard Lugar of Indiana.

Nunn and Lugar were authors of the U.S. Nunn-Lugar law under which the Washington has provided some $750 million to Russia over the last five years to help destroy and protect Cold War nuclear arsenals under START-1.

That treaty will soon take the U.S. and Russian nuclear arsenals down to 6,000 long-range warheads on each side. During the Cold War, the United States and Soviet Union each had more than 10,000 long-range nuclear warheads.

But the proposed START-2 treaty, which would slash U.S. and Russian strategic arsenals to about 3,000 warheads each by 2003, is in trouble in Russia, where there is deep suspicion of the cost and of planned NATO enlargement into Eastern Europe.

The U.S. Senate approved the treaty earlier this year, but Perry apparently had little success in an attempt on Thursday to persuade the Russian State Duma, the lower house of parliament, to follow suit.

Start-2 would eliminate Russia's big multiple-warhead SS-18 land-based intercontinental missiles and leave each country with only retaliatory single-warhead land-based missiles and multiple-warhead missiles based aboard submarines.

Perry told Duma members that bringing the arsenals down to a third of Cold War levels would save each country more than $4 billion in defence spending over the next five years and that the United States would provide Nunn-Lugar funds to help with the cuts.
During his three-day visit, Perry also held talks with Russian Defence Minister Igor Rodionov and Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin on bilateral and other military matters.

Perry said on Thursday that the sacking of Russian security chief Alexander Lebed by Russian President Boris Yeltsin would have no effect on what he called "strong and growing" military relations between Washington and Moscow.
Rodionov, who endorsed START-2 this week, and Perry are scheduled to meet in Bosnia in late November and again in Washington in December.
